stages.name: Corporate Phishing Foothold
observables: Phishing emails targeting Sales or Finance departments
Execution of malicious attachments on corporate laptops

stages.name: Compromised Third-Party Vendor Access
observables: Use of stolen credentials from specialized machine integrators or HVAC contractors
Persistent 'always-on' VPN links from vendor networks
Remote management tool logins appearing as routine maintenance

stages.name: IT-to-OT Bridge Access
observables: Access to Citrix or VPN appliances acting as bridges
Logins to jump servers positioned between corporate and plant networks
Stolen credentials used to cross network segmentation boundaries

stages.name: Legacy Industrial Asset Discovery
observables: Windows 7 and Windows XP systems running as HMIs
Legacy PLCs with hard-coded passwords like '1234' or 'password'
Unencrypted management ports active on legacy execution systems

stages.name: Lateral Movement via Tunneling
observables: Encapsulated network traffic traversing segment digital walls
Lateral movement using Telnet (port 23), FTP (port 21), or unencrypted HTTP (port 80)
Connections to Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs)

stages.name: Operational Technology Ransomware Impact
observables: Encryption of files on Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES)
Manipulation of PLC recipe values or belt speed
Disabling of safety sensors on the plant floor

scenario.summary: Attackers target manufacturing environments by gaining a corporate foothold via phishing or compromised third-party vendor VPNs, subsequently pivoting into operational technology (OT) networks through jump servers or poorly segmented bridges. Once inside, they exploit legacy systems and unencrypted protocols (Telnet, HTTP) to manipulate industrial control systems or deploy ransomware that disrupts production uptime and assembly lines.

meta.rationale: Focus on servers identified as VPN concentrators or IT/OT jump servers. The vendor_accounts list should be populated with the names of external contractors who have remote access privileges.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has breached a manufacturing network by using stolen vendor credentials on a VPN gateway or by exploiting a phishing foothold to traverse an IT-to-OT jump server.

hunt.name: Abuse of Remote Gateways and Third-Party Access
hunt.description: Manufacturing networks are increasingly targeted through their remote access infrastructure. Adversaries exploit stolen vendor credentials or phishing footholds to traverse the IT-to-OT bridge and halt production. This hunt identifies successful but anomalous sign-ins from third-party accounts. It then fans out to find evidence of the preceding compromise on corporate laptops and subsequent lateral probing from the gateway into the internal network. An agent weighs these results to determine if an intruder has bridged the network segments.

config.scoping_notes: Focus on servers identified as VPN concentrators or IT/OT jump servers. The vendor_accounts list should be populated with the names of external contractors who have remote access privileges.
config.beyond_detection: A standard rule alerts on a single login or shell; this hunt correlates a successful third-party login with its preceding foothold and its rare follow-on network connections, providing the context needed to distinguish maintenance from an intrusion.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, logon_type, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND ( (instr(',' || '{{vendor_accounts}}' || ',', ',' || (CASE WHEN instr(actor_user_name, '\') > 0 THEN SUBSTR(LOWER(actor_user_name), instr(actor_user_name, '\') + 1) ELSE LOWER(actor_user_name) END) || ',') > 0) OR (LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%vpn%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%gateway%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%jump%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%citrix%') OR (instr(',' || '{{gateway_keywords}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) || ',') > 0) ) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify successful authentications to gateways from vendor accounts or to specific gateway hostnames, handling domain prefixes and partial matches.
config.expected_signal: Rows show successful logins to critical gateways. Silence means no monitored accounts or services were accessed during the window.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\outlook.exe' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\chrome.exe' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\msedge.exe' OR instr(',' || '{{corporate_apps}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(parent_process_name) || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\powershell.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\cmd.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\wscript.exe' OR instr(',' || '{{interpreters}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify potential initial compromise on corporate machines where malicious payloads spawn shells, using partial path matching for robust detection.
config.expected_signal: Processes like PowerShell or CMD spawned directly from Outlook or a browser. Silence indicates no obvious script-based payloads ran from common entry apps.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, COUNT(*) AS connection_count FROM hb_network_connection WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND direction = 'outbound' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port HAVING connection_count < {{connection_threshold}} ORDER BY connection_count ASC
config.description: Detect bridging behavior where a gateway host initiates rare outbound connections to internal segments, using a tunable threshold.
config.expected_signal: Rare outbound connections from gateway machines to internal IP addresses. Silence suggests no anomalous probing from the identified gateways.
